---
title: "Immediate Conformity (Day 0)"
subtitle: "Baseline risk preferences and immediate conformity to social norms across moral and monetary domains"
author: "Przemek Marcowski"
---

This notebook analyzes baseline risk preferences and immediate conformity to social norms across Experiment 1 (moral domain: animal lives) and Experiment 2 (monetary domain: dollars), as well as the pooled cross-domain comparison. On each trial, participants chose between a sure outcome (saving or losing 10 lives or dollars for sure) and a 50/50 gamble of varying expected value under gain or loss framing, before and after learning a risk-averse or risk-seeking group norm.

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(glmmTMB)
library(emmeans)
library(easystats)
library(patchwork)
library(ggsignif)
library(here)

here::i_am("analysis/day0.qmd")
set.seed(42)
dir.create(here("output"), showWarnings = FALSE)

# Define factor levels for consistent ordering
PHASE_LEVELS <- c("Baseline", "OwnD0")
CONDITION_LEVELS <- c("Risk Averse", "Risk Seeking")
DOMAIN_LEVELS <- c("Gains", "Losses")
FRAME_LEVELS <- c("Lives", "Money")

fmt_num <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  x <- ifelse(abs(x) < 0.5 * 10^(-digits), 0, x)
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), x)
}

fmt_p <- function(p) {
  ifelse(p < 0.001, "< .001", sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p)))
}

fmt_conformity_table <- function(phase_df, pair_df, phase_label = "OwnD0") {
  bind_rows(
    phase_df %>%
      transmute(
        domain = factor(domain, levels = DOMAIN_LEVELS),
        ord = if_else(condition == "Risk Averse", 1L, 2L),
        Contrast = paste0(condition, " (", phase_label, " \u2212 Baseline)"),
        estimate, asymp.LCL, asymp.UCL, z.ratio, p.value
      ),
    pair_df %>%
      transmute(
        domain = factor(domain, levels = DOMAIN_LEVELS),
        ord = 3L,
        Contrast = "Norm asymmetry (Risk Averse \u2212 Risk Seeking)",
        estimate, asymp.LCL, asymp.UCL, z.ratio, p.value
      )
  ) %>%
    arrange(domain, ord) %>%
    transmute(
      Domain = as.character(domain),
      Contrast = Contrast,
      `ΔP [95% CI]` = sprintf("%s [%s, %s]", fmt_num(estimate), fmt_num(asymp.LCL), fmt_num(asymp.UCL)),
      z = fmt_num(z.ratio),
      p = fmt_p(p.value)
    ) %>%
    knitr::kable(align = "llrrr")
}
```

# Sample & Model Fitting

Each experiment is analyzed across the baseline and immediate post-exposure assessment phases.

```{r load-data}
# Load Experiment 1 data (Lives frame)
e1_data <- readRDS(here("data/experiment1.Rds")) %>%
  filter(time == "Dayone", phase %in% PHASE_LEVELS) %>%
  mutate(
    condition = factor(condition, levels = CONDITION_LEVELS),
    phase = factor(phase, levels = PHASE_LEVELS),
    domain = factor(domain, levels = DOMAIN_LEVELS)
  ) %>%
  select(-age)

# Load Experiment 2 data (Money frame)
e2_data <- readRDS(here("data/experiment2.Rds")) %>%
  filter(time == "Dayone", phase %in% PHASE_LEVELS) %>%
  mutate(
    condition = factor(condition, levels = CONDITION_LEVELS),
    phase = factor(phase, levels = PHASE_LEVELS),
    domain = factor(domain, levels = DOMAIN_LEVELS)
  ) %>%
  select(-age)

# Combine both experiments for joint analysis
combined_data <- bind_rows(e1_data, e2_data) %>%
  mutate(frame = factor(frame, levels = FRAME_LEVELS))

# Sample size by experiment, framing domain, and norm condition
sample_size_by_frame <- combined_data %>%
  group_by(frame, domain, condition) %>%
  summarize(n = n_distinct(id), .groups = "drop")

sample_size_by_frame %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = n) %>%
  mutate(
    Experiment = if_else(frame == "Lives", "Experiment 1 (Lives)", "Experiment 2 (Money)"),
    Domain = as.character(domain),
    Total = `Risk Averse` + `Risk Seeking`
  ) %>%
  select(Experiment, Domain, `Risk Averse`, `Risk Seeking`, Total) %>%
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrr")
```

We fit mixed-effects logistic regression models predicting binary gamble acceptance from expected value, assessment phase, norm condition, and framing domain (plus decision frame in the pooled model), with random intercepts for participants.

```{r model-fitting}
# Model formulas
e1_formula <- formula(choice ~ ev * phase * condition * domain + (1 | id))
e2_formula <- formula(choice ~ ev * phase * condition * domain + (1 | id))
combined_formula <- formula(choice ~ ev * phase * condition * domain * frame + (1 | id))

# Model control parameters
model_control <- glmmTMBControl(
  optCtrl = list(iter.max = 1e+3, eval.max = 1e+3),
  parallel = min(4L, max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 1L))
)

model_file_path <- here("output/models_day0.Rds")

if (!file.exists(model_file_path)) {
  e1_model <- glmmTMB(
    e1_formula, data = e1_data,
    family = binomial(link = "logit"),
    control = model_control
  )

  e2_model <- glmmTMB(
    e2_formula, data = e2_data,
    family = binomial(link = "logit"),
    control = model_control
  )

  combined_model <- glmmTMB(
    combined_formula, data = combined_data,
    family = binomial(link = "logit"),
    control = model_control
  )

  models <- list(e1_model, e2_model, combined_model)
  saveRDS(models, file = model_file_path)
} else {
  models <- readRDS(file = model_file_path)
  e1_model <- models[[1]]
  e2_model <- models[[2]]
  combined_model <- models[[3]]
}
```

# Experiment 1: Moral Domain (Lives)

In Experiment 1, we first evaluate sensitivity to expected value within each framing domain, overall baseline gambling against chance, and framing differences at baseline and immediate re-test.

```{r e1-baseline-and-domains}
# Standardized slopes of expected value by domain
e1_domain_slopes <- as.data.frame(standardize(estimate_slopes(e1_model, trend = "ev", by = "domain")))

# Overall gambling behavior at baseline against 0.5
e1_baseline_gambling <- broom::tidy(binom.test(
  sum(e1_data[e1_data$phase == "Baseline", "choice"]),
  nrow(e1_data[e1_data$phase == "Baseline", "choice"])
))

# Pairwise comparisons between domains (Losses vs. Gains) for each phase
e1_domain_comparisons <- withr::with_seed(42, emmeans(
  e1_model, revpairwise ~ domain | phase,
  regrid = "response", infer = TRUE, adjust = "mvt"
))
e1_domain_comp_df <- as.data.frame(e1_domain_comparisons$contrasts)
```

Participants tracked expected value in both domains, becoming more likely to gamble as expected lives saved increased in Gains (*b* = 0.10, 95% CI [0.09, 0.12], *z* = 13.20, *p* < .001) and less likely to gamble as expected lives lost increased in Losses (*b* = -0.16, 95% CI [-0.17, -0.14], *z* = -23.99, *p* < .001). Overall baseline gamble acceptance was below chance at 42.6% (95% CI [41.4%, 43.8%], *p* < .001), with a pronounced framing effect: participants gambled substantially more in Losses than in Gains both at baseline (Δ*P* = 0.32, 95% CI [0.16, 0.48], *z* = 3.96, *p* < .001) and at immediate re-test (Δ*P* = 0.24, 95% CI [0.09, 0.38], *z* = 3.25, *p* = .001).

Next, we test differences between the risk-averse and risk-seeking conditions within each phase and domain, the within-condition conformity shifts from baseline to immediate re-test, and the interaction contrast comparing the magnitude of risk-averse versus risk-seeking social influence.

```{r e1-conformity-contrasts}
# Pairwise comparisons between conditions for each phase and domain
e1_condition_comparisons <- as.data.frame(
  withr::with_seed(42, emmeans(
    e1_model, pairwise ~ condition | phase | domain,
    regrid = "response", infer = TRUE, adjust = "mvt",
    data = e1_data
  ))$contrasts
)

# Marginal means and phase contrasts (OwnD0 - Baseline) by condition and domain
e1_emmeans <- withr::with_seed(42, emmeans(
  e1_model, revpairwise ~ phase | condition | domain,
  regrid = "response", infer = TRUE, adjust = "mvt"
))
e1_emmeans_df <- as.data.frame(e1_emmeans$emmeans)
e1_contrasts_df <- as.data.frame(e1_emmeans$contrasts) %>%
  mutate(p_lab = cut(p.value, c(-Inf, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, Inf), labels = c("***", "**", "*", "ns")))
e1_contrasts_subset <- e1_contrasts_df[grepl("OwnD0 - Baseline", e1_contrasts_df$contrast), ]

# Predicted probabilities across the EV continuum
e1_predicted_probs <- estimate_means(
  e1_model,
  by = c("phase", "condition", "domain", "ev"),
  length = 100
)

# Contrasts of contrasts: Risk Averse shift vs. Risk Seeking shift
e1_conds_emmeans <- emmeans(
  e1_model, ~ condition * phase | domain,
  regrid = "response",
  at = list(phase = c("OwnD0", "Baseline"))
)

e1_contrasts <- contrast(
  e1_conds_emmeans,
  list(
    `Baseline Risk Averse - OwnD0 Risk Averse` = c(-1, 0, 1, 0),
    `OwnD0 Risk Seeking - Baseline Risk Seeking` = c(0, 1, 0, -1)
  )
)

e1_contrast_pairs <- as.data.frame(pairs(e1_contrasts, infer = TRUE))
e1_contrast_pairs$frame <- "Lives"
e1_contrast_pairs$p_sig <- with(e1_contrast_pairs, ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
e1_contrast_pairs$p_lab <- with(
  e1_contrast_pairs,
  cut(p.value, c(-Inf, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, Inf), labels = c("***", "**", "*", "ns"))
)
e1_contrast_pairs$x <- 1
e1_contrast_pairs$xend <- 2
e1_contrast_pairs$y <- 0.45

fmt_conformity_table(e1_contrasts_subset, e1_contrast_pairs, "OwnD0")
```

Before norm exposure, baseline gamble acceptance did not differ between the Risk Averse and Risk Seeking groups in either Gains (Δ*P* = 0.05, 95% CI [-0.10, 0.20], *z* = 0.63, *p* = .532) or Losses (Δ*P* = -0.06, 95% CI [-0.34, 0.22], *z* = -0.41, *p* = .680). After observing the group norm, the two conditions diverged sharply in both Gains (Δ*P* = -0.32, 95% CI [-0.51, -0.13], *z* = -3.28, *p* = .001) and Losses (Δ*P* = -0.51, 95% CI [-0.73, -0.30], *z* = -4.74, *p* < .001). Both risk-averse and risk-seeking norms shifted moral choices in the norm-consistent direction across both frames. In Losses, risk-averse norms exerted a stronger pull than risk-seeking norms, whereas in Gains the two norms were comparably effective.

```{r fig2}

(d) Marginal difference in gambling probability (OwnD0 minus Baseline) by condition and domain."

# Probability by EV plot
e1_prob_data <- e1_predicted_probs

e1_prob_plot <- ggplot(e1_prob_data, aes(x = ev, y = Probability, color = condition, fill = condition)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +

  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = CI_low, ymax = CI_high), alpha = 0.45, color = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, linetype = "solid") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Risk Averse" = "#262626", "Risk Seeking" = "#8C8C8C")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Risk Averse" = "#5C5C5C", "Risk Seeking" = "#CCCCCC")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  cowplot::theme_cowplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Gamble Acceptance by Expected Value",
    x = "Gamble Expected Value (Lives)",
    y = "Probability of Choosing the Gamble Option",
    color = "Condition",
    fill = "Condition",
    linetype = "Condition"
  ) +
  facet_grid(phase ~ domain, scales = "free_x") +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.justification = c(0.5, 0.5),
    panel.spacing = unit(1.2, "lines"),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black"),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent")
  )

# Difference plot by EV
e1_baseline_data <- e1_predicted_probs[e1_predicted_probs$phase == "Baseline", ]
e1_own0_data <- e1_predicted_probs[e1_predicted_probs$phase == "OwnD0", ]

e1_diffs <- e1_own0_data
e1_diffs$predicted <- e1_own0_data$Probability - e1_baseline_data$Probability
e1_diffs$conf.low <- e1_own0_data$CI_low - e1_baseline_data$CI_low
e1_diffs$conf.high <- e1_own0_data$CI_high - e1_baseline_data$CI_high
e1_diffs$contrast <- "OwnD0 - Baseline"

e1_prob_diffs_plot <- ggplot(e1_diffs, aes(x = ev, y = predicted, color = condition, fill = condition)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +

  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("solid", "dotted")) +
  scale_color_grey() +
  scale_fill_grey() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.5, 0.5)) +
  cowplot::theme_cowplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Influence by Expected Value",
    x = "Gamble Expected Value (Lives)",
    y = "Difference in Probabilities of Gambling\n(OwnD0 - Baseline)",
    color = "Condition",
    fill = "Condition",
    linetype = "Condition"
  ) +
  facet_grid(contrast ~ domain) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.justification = c(0.5, 0.5),
    legend.key.width = unit(2, "lines"),
    panel.spacing = unit(1.2, "lines"),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black"),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent")
  )

# Group probability plot
e1_group_plot <- ggplot(e1_emmeans_df, aes(x = phase, y = prob, fill = condition)) +

    title = "Gamble Acceptance by Phase",
    x = "Phase",
    y = "Probability of Choosing the Gamble Option",

    legend.justification = c(0.5, 0.5),

# Group difference plot
e1_group_diffs_plot <- ggplot(e1_contrasts_subset, aes(x = condition, y = estimate, fill = condition)) +
```

# Experiment 2: Monetary Domain (Money)

In Experiment 2, we evaluate sensitivity to expected value by framing domain, overall baseline gambling against chance, and framing contrasts at baseline and immediate re-test.

```{r e2-baseline-and-domains}
# Standardized slopes of expected value by domain
e2_domain_slopes <- as.data.frame(standardize(estimate_slopes(e2_model, trend = "ev", by = "domain")))

# Overall gambling behavior at baseline against 0.5
e2_baseline_gambling <- broom::tidy(binom.test(
  sum(e2_data[e2_data$phase == "Baseline", "choice"]),
  nrow(e2_data[e2_data$phase == "Baseline", "choice"])
))

# Pairwise comparisons between domains (Losses vs. Gains) for each phase
e2_domain_comparisons <- withr::with_seed(42, emmeans(
  e2_model, revpairwise ~ domain | phase,
  regrid = "response", infer = TRUE, adjust = "mvt"
))
e2_domain_comp_df <- as.data.frame(e2_domain_comparisons$contrasts)
```

Participants in the monetary domain likewise tracked expected value in both Gains (*b* = 0.15, 95% CI [0.14, 0.16], *z* = 30.70, *p* < .001) and Losses (*b* = -0.10, 95% CI [-0.11, -0.09], *z* = -24.81, *p* < .001). Overall baseline gambling did not differ from chance at 49.5% (95% CI [48.2%, 50.7%], *p* = .374), but showed the classic framing asymmetry: gamble acceptance was significantly higher in Losses than in Gains at baseline (Δ*P* = 0.30, 95% CI [0.17, 0.42], *z* = 4.62, *p* < .001), a difference that narrowed after norm exposure (Δ*P* = 0.07, 95% CI [-0.05, 0.19], *z* = 1.12, *p* = .261).

We then test differences between the risk-averse and risk-seeking conditions, within-condition conformity shifts from baseline to immediate re-test, and the interaction contrast comparing risk-averse and risk-seeking norm influence in monetary decisions.

```{r e2-conformity-contrasts}
# Pairwise comparisons between conditions for each phase and domain
e2_condition_comparisons <- as.data.frame(
  withr::with_seed(42, emmeans(
    e2_model, pairwise ~ condition | phase | domain,
    regrid = "response", infer = TRUE, adjust = "mvt"
  ))$contrasts
)

# Marginal means and phase contrasts (OwnD0 - Baseline) by condition and domain
e2_emmeans <- withr::with_seed(42, emmeans(
  e2_model, revpairwise ~ phase | condition | domain,
  regrid = "response", infer = TRUE, adjust = "mvt"
))
e2_emmeans_df <- as.data.frame(e2_emmeans$emmeans)
e2_contrasts_df <- as.data.frame(e2_emmeans$contrasts) %>%
  mutate(p_lab = cut(p.value, c(-Inf, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, Inf), labels = c("***", "**", "*", "ns")))
e2_contrasts_subset <- e2_contrasts_df[grepl("OwnD0 - Baseline", e2_contrasts_df$contrast), ]

# Predicted probabilities across the EV continuum
e2_predicted_probs <- estimate_means(
  e2_model,
  by = c("phase", "condition", "domain", "ev"),
  length = 100
)

# Contrasts of contrasts: Risk Averse shift vs. Risk Seeking shift
e2_conds_emmeans <- emmeans(
  e2_model, ~ condition * phase | domain,
  regrid = "response",
  at = list(phase = c("OwnD0", "Baseline"))
)

e2_contrasts <- contrast(
  e2_conds_emmeans,
  list(
    `Baseline Risk Averse - OwnD0 Risk Averse` = c(-1, 0, 1, 0),
    `OwnD0 Risk Seeking - Baseline Risk Seeking` = c(0, 1, 0, -1)
  )
)

e2_contrast_pairs <- as.data.frame(pairs(e2_contrasts, infer = TRUE))
e2_contrast_pairs$frame <- "Money"
e2_contrast_pairs$p_sig <- with(e2_contrast_pairs, ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))
e2_contrast_pairs$p_lab <- with(
  e2_contrast_pairs,
  cut(p.value, c(-Inf, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, Inf), labels = c("***", "**", "*", "ns"))
)
e2_contrast_pairs$x <- 1
e2_contrast_pairs$xend <- 2
e2_contrast_pairs$y <- 0.45

# Combine contrast pairs across both experiments
all_contrast_pairs <- rbind(e1_contrast_pairs, e2_contrast_pairs)

fmt_conformity_table(e2_contrasts_subset, e2_contrast_pairs, "OwnD0")
```

At baseline, gamble acceptance did not differ between conditions in either Gains (Δ*P* = -0.10, 95% CI [-0.27, 0.06], *z* = -1.20, *p* = .229) or Losses (Δ*P* = -0.07, 95% CI [-0.26, 0.12], *z* = -0.73, *p* = .468), whereas after norm exposure the two conditions differed strongly in both Gains (Δ*P* = -0.40, 95% CI [-0.55, -0.24], *z* = -4.97, *p* < .001) and Losses (Δ*P* = -0.34, 95% CI [-0.52, -0.16], *z* = -3.63, *p* < .001). Conformity in the monetary domain was sharpest when the norm opposed default framing tendencies: risk-seeking norms produced a large shift in Gains while risk-averse norms produced only a marginal shift, whereas in Losses risk-averse norms produced a large shift while risk-seeking norms did not move choices from baseline.

```{r fig4}
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, linetype = "solid") +

  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  cowplot::theme_cowplot() +
  labs(
```

# Combined Analysis: Moral vs. Monetary Domains

Pooling Experiment 1 and Experiment 2, we compare post-exposure gamble acceptance and the magnitude of norm influence directly between moral and monetary frames.

```{r combined-contrasts}
# Standardized slopes of expected value by domain in the pooled model
combined_slopes <- as.data.frame(standardize(estimate_slopes(combined_model, trend = "ev", by = "domain")))

# Marginal means and Money - Lives contrasts at OwnD0
combined_emmeans <- withr::with_seed(42, emmeans(
  combined_model, revpairwise ~ frame | phase | condition | domain,
  regrid = "response", infer = TRUE, adjust = "mvt",
  at = list(phase = "OwnD0")
))
combined_emmeans_df <- as.data.frame(combined_emmeans$emmeans)
combined_contrasts_df <- as.data.frame(combined_emmeans$contrasts) %>%
  mutate(p_lab = cut(p.value, c(-Inf, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, Inf), labels = c("***", "**", "*", "ns")))

# Frame x phase x condition interactions within each domain
combined_conds_emmeans <- emmeans(
  combined_model, ~ frame * phase * condition | domain,
  regrid = "response",
  at = list(phase = c("OwnD0", "Baseline"))
)

combined_contrasts <- contrast(
  combined_conds_emmeans,
  list(
    `Baseline Risk Averse [Lives] - OwnD0 Risk Averse [Lives]` = c(-1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
    `Baseline Risk Averse [Money] - OwnD0 Risk Averse [Money]` = c(0, -1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0),
    `OwnD0 Risk Seeking [Lives] - Baseline Risk Seeking [Lives]` = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, -1, 0),
    `OwnD0 Risk Seeking [Money] - Baseline Risk Seeking [Money]` = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, -1)
  )
)

# Frame differences (Money - Lives) by condition
frame_by_condition_contrast <- contrast(
  combined_contrasts,
  list(
    `Money - Lives [Risk Averse]` = c(-1, 1, 0, 0),
    `Money - Lives [Risk Seeking]` = c(0, 0, -1, 1)
  ),
  infer = TRUE
)

frame_condition_pairs <- as.data.frame(frame_by_condition_contrast)
frame_condition_pairs$condition <- with(
  frame_condition_pairs,
  str_remove_all(str_extract(contrast, "\\[.+\\]"), "\\[|\\]")
)
frame_condition_pairs$p_sig <- with(
  frame_condition_pairs,
  ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", "")
)
frame_condition_pairs$p_lab <- with(
  frame_condition_pairs,
  cut(p.value, c(-Inf, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, Inf), labels = c("***", "**", "*", "ns"))
)

# Condition asymmetry differences (Risk Averse - Risk Seeking) by frame
condition_by_frame_contrast <- contrast(
  combined_contrasts,
  list(
    `Risk Averse [Lives] - Risk Seeking [Lives]` = c(1, 0, -1, 0),
    `Risk Averse [Money] - Risk Seeking [Money]` = c(0, 1, 0, -1)
  ),
  infer = TRUE
)

condition_frame_pairs <- pairs(condition_by_frame_contrast, infer = TRUE)
condition_frame_pairs_df <- as.data.frame(condition_frame_pairs)
condition_frame_pairs_df$p_sig <- with(
  condition_frame_pairs_df,
  ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", "")
)
condition_frame_pairs_df$p_lab <- with(
  condition_frame_pairs_df,
  cut(p.value, c(-Inf, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, Inf), labels = c("***", "**", "*", "ns"))
)
condition_frame_pairs_df$x <- 1
condition_frame_pairs_df$xend <- 2
condition_frame_pairs_df$y <- 0.45

# Domain by frame contrast at baseline
domain_frame_contrast <- emmeans(
  combined_model, ~ domain * frame,
  regrid = "response",
  at = list(phase = c("Baseline"))
)

domain_frame_contrast_pairs <- contrast(
  domain_frame_contrast,
  list(
    `Gains - Losses [Lives]` = c(1, -1, 0, 0),
    `Gains - Losses [Money]` = c(0, 0, 1, -1)
  ),
  infer = TRUE
)

domain_frame_pairs <- as.data.frame(pairs(domain_frame_contrast_pairs, infer = TRUE))

bind_rows(
  frame_condition_pairs %>%
    transmute(
      domain = factor(domain, levels = DOMAIN_LEVELS),
      ord = if_else(condition == "Risk Averse", 1L, 2L),
      Contrast = paste0(condition, " shift (Money \u2212 Lives)"),
      estimate, asymp.LCL, asymp.UCL, z.ratio, p.value
    ),
  condition_frame_pairs_df %>%
    transmute(
      domain = factor(domain, levels = DOMAIN_LEVELS),
      ord = 3L,
      Contrast = "Norm asymmetry (Lives \u2212 Money)",
      estimate, asymp.LCL, asymp.UCL, z.ratio, p.value
    )
) %>%
  arrange(domain, ord) %>%
  transmute(
    Domain = as.character(domain),
    Contrast = Contrast,
    `ΔP [95% CI]` = sprintf("%s [%s, %s]", fmt_num(estimate), fmt_num(asymp.LCL), fmt_num(asymp.UCL)),
    z = fmt_num(z.ratio),
    p = fmt_p(p.value)
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrr")
```

Across the pooled sample, expected value strongly predicted choice in both Gains (*b* = 0.13, 95% CI [0.12, 0.14], *z* = 27.37, *p* < .001) and Losses (*b* = -0.13, 95% CI [-0.14, -0.12], *z* = -33.19, *p* < .001), and the magnitude of the baseline gain-loss framing effect did not differ significantly between moral and monetary frames (Δ*P* = 0.14, 95% CI [-0.06, 0.34], *z* = 1.35, *p* = .178). At immediate re-test, overall gamble acceptance was higher for money than for animal lives under risk-averse norms in both Gains (Δ*P* = 0.20, 95% CI [0.10, 0.29], *z* = 3.89, *p* < .001) and Losses (Δ*P* = 0.26, 95% CI [0.08, 0.45], *z* = 2.77, *p* = .006), whereas post-exposure gamble acceptance under risk-seeking norms did not differ significantly between frames in Gains (Δ*P* = 0.22, 95% CI [-0.02, 0.45], *z* = 1.79, *p* = .073) or Losses (Δ*P* = 0.14, 95% CI [-0.08, 0.36], *z* = 1.22, *p* = .224). Comparing conformity shifts directly across frames shows that risk-averse norms exerted stronger influence in moral than in monetary Gains, whereas risk-seeking norms exerted stronger influence in moral than in monetary Losses.
